text: Regular expressions let you search and manipulate text using powerful patterns instead of exact strings.
The re module is Python's built-in engine for these patterns.
findall scans the text and returns every substring matching your pattern — here, email addresses.
[chuckle] The pattern reads: some word characters, an at-sign, then more word characters — the shape of an email.
[sniff] search finds the first match, and parentheses create groups you can pull out individually.
This pattern captures a phone number as two separate pieces, the prefix and the line number.
[sigh] And sub replaces every match with new text — here collapsing runs of whitespace into a single space.
Regex is dense and cryptic at first, but incredibly powerful once the symbols click.
[groan] Learn a few core patterns, and text cleaning and extraction that once took loops becomes a single line.
